title: File System
prompt: Design an in-memory hierarchical file system. Implement classes to support: mkdir (create directories), ls (list contents), addContentToFile (create/append to a file), and readContentFromFile (read a file). All operations work with absolute paths like /a/b/c. Paths may have intermediate directories that don't exist — mkdir creates them implicitly.

stages.title: Requirements
stages.questionPrompt: Clarify the requirements. What's in scope and what isn't?
stages.howToAnswer: Capture the rules tightly. Decide whether to scope: symbolic links, permissions, file deletion, disk quotas. State assumptions about path formats and case sensitivity.

exampleHints.headline: Example (Movie Theater):
bullets: Create directories recursively along a path (mkdir /a/b/c)
List files and directories at a path, lexicographically sorted (ls /a/b)
Create or append content to a file (addContentToFile /a/file.txt, content)
Read the full content of a file (readContentFromFile /a/file.txt)
Out of Scope: symbolic links, permissions, deletion, disk quotas

must: mkdir creates directories; intermediate dirs auto-created if needed
ls returns sorted names of files and directories in a given directory
addContentToFile creates a file or appends to existing; auto-creates parent dirs
readContentFromFile returns file content as a single string
Path format: absolute paths like /a/b/c; root is /
should: Return meaningful errors for invalid operations (file as directory, reading non-existent file)
Support empty files and empty content appends
avoid: Designing a UI or persistence layer

stages.sampleAnswer:
Scope:
- mkdir(path): create directories along path, auto-creating intermediates
- ls(path): return sorted list of file/dir names at path; if path is a file, return [filename]
- addContentToFile(path, content): create file with content or append to existing; auto-create parent dirs
- readContentFromFile(path): return full file content
- Path format: absolute paths, root is /

Out of Scope:
- Deletion, move/rename
- Symbolic links, hard links
- Permissions, ownership
- Disk quotas or size limits
- Concurrency control
hints: Start by clarifying what the core operations do: is mkdir idempotent? Does addContentToFile auto-create parent dirs?
Decide on the path format once. How do you parse /a/b/c into components?
Out of scope: don't build deletion or permission layers unless the interviewer asks.

stages.title: Entities & Relationships
stages.questionPrompt: What are the core entities and how do they relate?
stages.howToAnswer: Pick the orchestrator. Decide what owns the file tree. Use an abstract Node class with File and Directory subclasses.

exampleHints.headline: Example (Elevator):
bullets: FileSystem (orchestrator)
Node (abstract base)
File (holds content)
Directory (holds children map)

must: FileSystem (orchestrator, holds root node, exposes ls/mkdir/etc)
Node abstract class or interface
File (subclass of Node, owns content string)
Directory (subclass of Node, owns Map<name, Node>)
Path resolution logic (walk from root)
should: Avoid storing full paths — store parent and name only
Directory.children keyed by name, not path
avoid: Putting all logic into FileSystem; File and Directory should know themselves
Storing absolute paths on every node

stages.sampleAnswer:
- FileSystem: orchestrates, holds root Directory, exposes mkdir/ls/addContentToFile/readContentFromFile.
- Node: abstract base class with name field.
- File: extends Node, owns content (string).
- Directory: extends Node, owns children (Map<String, Node>).
- Path resolution: split path by '/', walk from root, create Directories as needed in mkdir.
hints: Should every node know its parent, or should you pass context down the tree?
Use a shared abstract class or interface so File and Directory both fit into the children Map.
Path resolution: write a helper that walks the tree and returns the target node (or None if missing).

stages.title: Class Design
stages.questionPrompt: Define the classes — fields and methods. Keep rules with the entity that owns the state.
stages.howToAnswer: Sketch each class with explicit method signatures. Return meaningful types: throw exceptions for invalid access (reading a dir, accessing non-existent path), return boolean for operations, return List for ls.

exampleHints.headline: Example (Parking Lot):
bullets: class FileSystem: + ls(path) -> List<String>, + mkdir(path) -> void, + addContentToFile(...) -> void, + readContentFromFile(path) -> String
class Node: name: String
class File(Node): content: String, + append(text) -> void
class Directory(Node): children: Map<String, Node>, + addChild(node) -> void, + getChild(name) -> Node?

must: FileSystem methods: ls, mkdir, addContentToFile, readContentFromFile with correct signatures
File and Directory as subclasses of Node
Directory.children is a Map keyed by name
Methods throw exceptions for invalid operations (e.g., readContentFromFile on a directory)
ls returns List<String>, sorted
avoid: Returning bool when you need to throw an exception
Exposing children map directly without encapsulation

stages.sampleAnswer:
```
abstract class Node:
  name: String
  constructor(name: String): ...

class File(Node):
  content: String = ""
  constructor(name: String): super(name)
  append(text: String): void
    content += text

class Directory(Node):
  children: Map<String, Node> = {}
  constructor(name: String): super(name)
  addChild(node: Node): void
    children[node.name] = node
  getChild(name: String): Node?
    return children[name]

class FileSystem:
  root: Directory = Directory("/")
  
  ls(path: String) -> List<String>:
    node = getNode(path)
    if node is File: return [node.name]
    if node is Directory: return sorted(node.children.keys())
    throw FileNotFound
  
  mkdir(path: String) -> void:
    ensurePath(path, createDirs=true)
  
  addContentToFile(path: String, content: String) -> void:
    ensurePath(parentPath(path), createDirs=true)
    file = getOrCreateFile(path)
    file.append(content)
  
  readContentFromFile(path: String) -> String:
    file = getNode(path)
    if file is not File: throw NotAFile
    return file.content
```
hints: Methods that modify the tree should return void or throw. Methods that read should return a value or throw.
ls is special: if path is a file, return just [filename]; if directory, return sorted child names.
Path resolution: split by '/', walk from root. What happens if a component is missing?

stages.title: Implementation
stages.questionPrompt: Pseudo-code path resolution and the core mkdir/addContentToFile logic. Trace through one scenario.
stages.howToAnswer: The meaty method is path resolution — write it carefully. Then trace a sequence: mkdir /a/b, addContentToFile /a/b/file.txt content, readContentFromFile /a/b/file.txt.

exampleHints.headline: Example (Parking Lot):
bullets: getNode(path): split path, walk tree from root, return node or None
ensurePath(path, createDirs): walk tree, creating Directory nodes as needed
addContentToFile: ensure parent dirs exist, then create File or append

must: Path resolution: split by '/', walk from root, validate at each step
mkdir: create intermediate Directory nodes if needed
addContentToFile: ensure parent dirs exist, create File or append to existing
Trace through one concrete scenario end-to-end
should: Single getNode(path) helper reused across methods
Explicit check: is this path a file or directory?
avoid: Silent failure on invalid paths — throw exceptions

stages.sampleAnswer:
```
getNode(path: String) -> Node?:
  parts = path.split('/').filter(p => p != '')
  current = root
  for part in parts:
    if current is File: return None  // can't traverse through a file
    if not current.children.contains(part): return None
    current = current.children[part]
  return current

ensurePath(path: String, createDirs: bool) -> Directory:
  parts = path.split('/').filter(p => p != '')
  current = root
  for part in parts:
    if current is File: throw NotADirectory
    if not current.children.contains(part):
      if not createDirs: throw FileNotFound
      newDir = Directory(part)
      current.addChild(newDir)
      current = newDir
    else:
      next = current.children[part]
      if next is File: throw NotADirectory  // path has a file in the middle
      current = next
  return current

mkdir(path: String) -> void:
  ensurePath(path, createDirs=true)

addContentToFile(path: String, content: String) -> void:
  parentPath = path.substring(0, path.lastIndexOf('/'))
  fileName = path.substring(path.lastIndexOf('/') + 1)
  if parentPath == '': parentPath = '/'
  
  parentDir = ensurePath(parentPath, createDirs=true)
  if parentDir.children.contains(fileName):
    node = parentDir.children[fileName]
    if node is Directory: throw NotAFile
    ((File) node).append(content)
  else:
    file = File(fileName)
    file.append(content)
    parentDir.addChild(file)

readContentFromFile(path: String) -> String:
  node = getNode(path)
  if node == None: throw FileNotFound
  if node is Directory: throw NotAFile
  return ((File) node).content

ls(path: String) -> List<String>:
  node = getNode(path)
  if node == None: throw FileNotFound
  if node is File: return [node.name]
  names = node.children.keySet()
  return names.sorted()
```

Trace: 
1. mkdir('/a/b'): ensurePath creates root->Directory('a')->Directory('b')
2. addContentToFile('/a/b/file.txt', 'hello'): ensurePath('/a/b') returns existing, creates File('file.txt'), appends 'hello'
3. addContentToFile('/a/b/file.txt', ' world'): getNode finds File, appends ' world' → content = 'hello world'
4. readContentFromFile('/a/b/file.txt'): getNode returns File, returns 'hello world'
5. ls('/a/b'): getNode returns Directory, returns ['file.txt']
hints: Write getNode and ensurePath first — they're the foundation. The rest builds on them.
Path handling: split by '/', ignore empty parts. Root path '/' has no parts.
Trace one full scenario: mkdir, add, read, ls. Catch off-by-one errors in path parsing.

stages.title: Extensibility
stages.questionPrompt: How would you extend this for: file deletion, move/rename, symbolic links, or permissions?
stages.howToAnswer: Stay high-level. Point at the seams in the design that make each extension clean.

exampleHints.headline: Example (Tic Tac Toe):
bullets: File deletion: add rm(path) method, Directory.removeChild(name)
Move/rename: swap node references in children maps or rename field
Symbolic links: new Link subclass of Node, points to another Node
Permissions: add perms field to Node, check before mkdir/read/write

must: File deletion: Directory.removeChild(name), rm(path) traverses and deletes
Move/rename: either swap children map entries or update node name and re-parent
should: Symbolic links: new Link(Node) subclass, getTarget() method, ensure no cycles
Permissions: add perms to Node, check in each operation's access path
avoid: Rewriting the tree structure for deletion or permissions
Storing full paths when parent pointers or name suffice

stages.sampleAnswer:
File deletion: add Directory.removeChild(name: String) -> void. rm(path) gets the parent directory and calls removeChild(filename). Cascading delete is implicit — the removed Directory's children are unreachable.

Move/rename: rename is easy if you add a setName(newName) method; move is harder. Option 1: parentDir.removeChild(oldName), then re-parent the node into newDir and update name. Option 2: track parent pointers on nodes, update in both directions.

Symbolic links: new Link(Node target) extends Node. When resolving a path, if you encounter a Link, follow link.getTarget() and continue from there. Detect cycles by tracking visited nodes in the resolution walk.

Permissions: add perms: Perms to every Node. Modify ls, mkdir, addContentToFile, readContentFromFile to check perms before proceeding. Perms can be { owner, group, rwx, ... } — just one more field on each Node.
hints: Where are the seams? Point at them: removeChild on Directory, a new Link subclass, a Perms field on Node.
Deletion is clean if Directory.children is well-encapsulated. What breaks if you expose it directly?
Symbolic links: what's the minimal contract you add to Node to make Link work? Just getTarget()?

deepDives.title: Path resolution and edge cases
deepDives.questionPrompt: How do you safely resolve a path like /a/b/c when some intermediate components are files? What exceptions do you throw and when?
deepDives.sampleAnswer: Path resolution is a walk from root, splitting by '/' and validating at each step. If you encounter a File node in the middle (e.g., /a/file.txt/b), you throw NotADirectoryException — you can't descend into a file. For mkdir and addContentToFile, you auto-create missing Directory nodes. For read operations (ls, readContentFromFile), if any component is missing, throw FileNotFoundException. The key is: validate type at each step and decide whether to auto-create or fail based on the operation.

must: Detect file-in-path and throw NotADirectoryException
Differentiate between missing components (auto-create for write, error for read) and invalid types
Consistent exception types across all operations
should: Note empty path (root) as special case
Mention what happens when path ends in '/' (canonical form)
avoid: Silently returning None or null — always throw or return Optional

hints: When you split /a/b/c by '/', you get [a, b, c]. How do you handle the case where a is actually a File?
Trace one concrete error: call mkdir('/file.txt/subdir') where /file.txt exists and is a file.
What's the minimal set of exceptions you need? FileNotFoundException, NotADirectoryException, NotAFileException?

deepDives.title: Thread safety
deepDives.questionPrompt: If multiple threads call mkdir, ls, and addContentToFile concurrently, where are the race conditions? How would you fix them?
deepDives.sampleAnswer: The FileSystem.root and all subtrees are shared mutable state. Two threads calling mkdir('/a'), both checking if 'a' exists and both creating it, is a classic race condition. Similarly, concurrent addContentToFile and readContentFromFile on the same file can tear the content string. The fix: wrap the entire FileSystem in a single ReentrantReadWriteLock. ls and readContentFromFile use read locks (multiple readers, no writers). mkdir, addContentToFile, and rm use write locks. Alternatively, lock at the node level (per-directory lock), but that's complex for path-wide atomicity.

must: Identify the shared state (tree structure and File.content)
Describe at least 2 race conditions (mkdir collision, content tear)
should: Propose a concrete synchronization mechanism (single lock, RWLock, per-node locks)
Discuss read vs write lock granularity
avoid: Ignoring content appends as a mutation

hints: Two threads both trying to mkdir('/a') for the first time — what goes wrong without locking?
One thread reads File.content while another appends. What do you see?
Is a read lock enough for ls? What about for reading a file that's being appended to?

deepDives.title: Recursive deletion
deepDives.questionPrompt: How would you implement rm(path) to delete a file or directory? What about cascading delete for nested directories?
deepDives.sampleAnswer: rm(path) traverses to the parent directory and calls parent.removeChild(name). For a File, this is trivial — the node is garbage-collected. For a Directory, removeChild just removes it from the parent's children map, rendering its entire subtree unreachable in one step. Java and Python automatically garbage-collect the unreachable subtree. There's no explicit recursive deletion needed — the design naturally handles it. Optionally, return boolean (true if deleted, false if not found) or return the deleted node for use in undo/redo.

must: Implement rm by calling parent.removeChild(name)
Explain why cascading deletion happens implicitly
should: Distinguish between rm /file (remove File) and rm /dir (remove Directory + children)
Return a useful value (boolean success, deleted node, or throw)
avoid: Implementing a recursive walk to manually delete each child

hints: After removing a Directory from its parent's children map, what happens to all nodes inside it?
Should rm fail on a non-empty directory, or succeed with cascading delete?
What return type makes sense: bool, the deleted Node, or an exception?
